coverage.method: Complete page-by-page extracted text read; rendered pages separately listed where inspected.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Constitution of Year III: property, rights and duties
findings.source_grounded_analysis: The constitution sought stability while retaining civil equality and property-based political authority, explicitly rejecting the 1793 model. A declaration of rights was balanced by duties; taxpayer citizenship and restricted second-stage electoral eligibility were distinct.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Year III constitution; citizenship; property franchise; Boissy d’Anglas; rights and duties
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Preserve narrator versus quoted advocacy and distinguish civil equality from social/economic equality.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: Five Hundred initiated legislation; Elders accepted or rejected it and chose Directors from a lower-house list. Annual renewal, separation from ministers, and slow amendment rules were intended as checks.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Council of Five Hundred; Council of Elders; Directory; separation of powers; constitutional amendment
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Check institutional powers and relationship direction, not merely a common constitution umbrella.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: Continuity for Convention deputies was designed to avoid 1791’s self-denial but frustrated public and royalist hopes. Constitutional acceptance and the disputed/ambiguous law vote must not be conflated. Many surviving deputies gained seats without election.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Two Thirds Law; constitutional referendum; Convention perpetuation; electoral assemblies
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Distinguish law from constitution and uncertain official tallies from complete popular consent.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Vendémiaire uprising: aims, suppression and consequence
findings.source_grounded_analysis: Sections opposed the law and electoral manipulation; their defeat involved prolonged fighting and hundreds of deaths, not merely Bonaparte’s celebrated few shots. Doyle does not regard their royalism as established. Army suppression ended Parisian coercion of representatives.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Vendémiaire uprising; Barras; Bonaparte; Paris sections; army in domestic politics
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Preserve uncertain political composition, local machinery and significance beyond Napoleon biography.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: The government alternately tolerated and suppressed Jacobins or royalists to maintain a republican middle; this was not consistent support of either wing. Its property-based constituency often preferred monarchy.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Directory political strategy; Jacobin revival; royalism; constitutional circles
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Track the chronology and limits of tolerated opposition rather than making all clubs government supporters.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: Section assemblies and their National Guard organization were replaced by centrally controlled institutions; later dissolution of the Police Legion further increased dependence on regular troops. Revolutionary journées became much harder to organize.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Paris sections abolition; Parisian Guard; Police Legion; army dependence
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Do not conflate successive forces or describe attempted coups as simply repeated sansculotte journées.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Assignat collapse, mandates and unequal effects
findings.source_grounded_analysis: Scarcity, requisitions, bad weather and blockade accompanied hyperinflation. Government was both debtor and tax creditor; private debtors and property speculators could gain. Failed land-bank plans and territorial mandates preceded demonetization, deflation, debtor hardship and barter.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: assignats; territorial mandates; land bank; inflation; deflation; national property speculation
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Separate paper currencies, stages and groups benefiting/losing; do not imply a smooth transition to financial stability.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: Ramel’s bank proposal failed; after Fructidor the Two Thirds Bankruptcy removed much debt service, but violated a long revolutionary commitment and hurt holders. Central collection and revived indirect taxation enabled longer-term recovery while alienating property owners.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Ramel; Two Thirds Bankruptcy; national debt; Agency for Direct Contributions; indirect taxes
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Keep immediate repudiation and delayed fiscal reconstruction distinct; include both political cost and institutional continuity.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Babeuf’s egalitarianism and Conspiracy of Equals
findings.source_grounded_analysis: Babeuf advocated common property and equal distribution but contemporaries responded more to the 1793 constitution. The conspiracy’s programme, infiltration strategy, missed Police Legion mutiny, betrayal, arrests and later trial were distinct from mass mobilization.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Babeuf; Tribun du peuple; communism; Equals; Buonarroti; constitution of 1793
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Do not automatically attribute Babeuf’s full doctrine to all Jacobins or all conspirators; retain proposed coercive methods.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Repression and attempted subversion of troops
findings.source_grounded_analysis: The Vendôme high-court trial and Grenelle march had different timing and judicial forms. Informants foiled left and later royalist troop-subversion attempts; Brottier’s trial ran beside Babeuf’s.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Vendôme trial; Grenelle incident; Brottier plot; military subversion; informers
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Avoid conflating conspiracies or treating their claimed soldier support as demonstrated.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Royalist electoral organization and internal divisions
findings.source_grounded_analysis: Clichy and the Philanthropic Institute cultivated propertied voters; legitimists, constitutionalists and Orleanists differed. Local southern vengeance lacked coherent national goals. The Blankenburg declaration offered only ambiguous concessions.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Clichy Club; Philanthropic Institute; Orleanism; White Terror; Blankenburg declaration
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Preserve faction boundaries and distinction between electoral organization and violent inner circles.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Year V elections and government electioneering
findings.source_grounded_analysis: Commissioners, émigré voting restrictions and anti-extremist oaths marked systematic official campaigning. The electorate rejected incumbents amid low participation; royalist success did not create a homogeneous restoration bloc.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Year V elections; directorial commissioners; voter restrictions; Barthélemy
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Do not equate anti-Directory votes, royalist labels and support for one restoration programme.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Fructidor coup and its contested necessity
findings.source_grounded_analysis: Conflict over peace, generals’ conquests, Pichegru’s treason and divided Directors led to military arrests, press closures and annulments. Doyle thinks a working moderate republican majority was possible and restoration prevention improbable; the coup discredited the constitution.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: 18 Fructidor; triumvirs; Augereau; Pichegru; Carnot; constitutional failure
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Retain author’s probabilistic judgment and distinguish royalist conspirators from all purged representatives.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: After Fructidor Austria settled while British negotiations failed. Bonaparte and Talleyrand proposed Egypt as an indirect blow to India; the Directors also wished the popular general abroad. Naval defeat stranded troops and helped create the Second Coalition.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Campo Formio; Britain peace negotiations; Egypt expedition; battle of Nile; Talleyrand
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Record intended commercial-strategic mechanism as a plan, not an achieved cutoff of India; reconcile source’s sailing-date discrepancy.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: Post-Fructidor measures targeted émigrés, formally deprived nobles of citizenship with little enforcement, and restored clerical penalties. Numbers refusing the oath, interned, embarked and reaching Guiana are different populations.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Directorial Terror; oath of hatred; clergy deportation; Ré; Oléron; Guiana; nobles citizenship
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Check scope and denominators; do not present unenforced noble disability as universal expulsion.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: Catholic recovery persisted after 1795; Grégoire sustained the constitutional Church. La Revellière sponsored Theophilanthropy, but neither it nor republican décadis commanded wide adherence.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Theophilanthropy; Grégoire; constitutional Church; religious revival; republican calendar
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Keep churches and cults separate and distinguish state sponsorship from popular acceptance.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: Constitutional circles included varied republicans; surveillance and closures preceded split electoral assemblies and executive verification. The Floréal law removed winners and substituted minorities, renewing executive control. Possible parliamentary opposition remains a historical interpretation.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: constitutional circles; neo-Jacobins; Rue du Bac; Year VI elections; 22 Floréal
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Preserve distinctions between circles, Jacobin winners, official candidates and historiographical conjecture.

findings.subject_or_distinction: Great Nation expansion and Second Coalition
findings.source_grounded_analysis: French claims of superiority and natural frontiers underwrote Rhine annexation, sister republics and interference in Rome/Switzerland. Egypt, Malta, papal imprisonment and Russian/Austrian/Neapolitan interests converged in renewed war; Championnet’s expansion exceeded policy.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Great Nation; natural frontiers; Rastadt; Helvetic/Roman/Parthenopean republics; Pius VI; Second Coalition
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Do not attribute every expansion to an ordered central plan; preserve separate foreign motivations.

findings.source_grounded_analysis: The law revived universal service obligation with volunteers first and annual classes of young men as needed. Renewed war and anticlericalism recalled earlier unpopular demands, eroding the prospect of stability and eventually military loyalty.
findings.reader_routes_to_check: Jourdan Law; conscription; annual military classes; Directory collapse
findings.eventual_draft_checks: Differentiate service principle, selection procedure and broader political consequences.

uncertainties.issue: Egyptian expedition departure is 19 May on p333 and 17 May on p338. Both appear in extracted source; retain discrepancy pending render if exact date is used.
